exposure: Expectant management after PPROM between 34+0 and 36+6 weeks of gestation
Presence or suspicion of intrauterine inflammation, infection, or both (TRIPLE-I) criteria (e.g., elevated white blood cell count, tachycardic cardiotocography)
outcome: Neonatal admission to NICU due to infection
cohort: This study included 323 singleton pregnancies with preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) between 34+0 and 36+6 weeks of gestation undergoing expectant management.
finding: Expectant management of PPROM between 34+0 and 36+6 weeks of gestation, even with suspicion of TRIPLE-I criteria, did not significantly increase the risk of adverse neonatal outcomes such as low umbilical artery pH, low Apgar score, or NICU admission due to infection.
gest_age: PPROM occurred between 34+0 and 36+6 weeks of gestation, with a mean gestational age at PPROM of 34.7 weeks and at birth of 35.9 weeks.
